labels.flagged_only_note: Item reports were written only for items with findings above informational (--item-reports flagged). Items without a link have no report folder: their status and finding counts are shown here.
labels.cancelled_note: The run was cancelled by the user; only the items processed before cancellation are reported.
labels.method_text: Each file was read once to compute its digests, then analysed as email: .eml as an RFC 5322 message, .msg through its MAPI properties, and each message of an mbox as an item of its own (each in a separate worker process with time and memory limits when worker isolation is on, as recorded in the audit log). The header section, Received hops and dates were read and compared; DKIM and ARC signatures were verified offline with the public keys the examiner supplied (no DNS query unless online mode was chosen); Authentication-Results were recorded as stated evidence; attachments were hashed; and BEC heuristics compared the addresses with the organisation's own domains. Every step and every file written is recorded in the hash-chained audit log.

EMPTY_FILE.title: Empty file
EMPTY_FILE.shows: The file contains no data (0 bytes).
EMPTY_FILE.does_not_prove: It does not show whether the file was emptied deliberately or created empty.

EXTENSION_MISMATCH.title: Extension does not match content
EXTENSION_MISMATCH.shows: The name ends in .%{extension} but the content starts with the signature of a %{detected} file.
EXTENSION_MISMATCH.does_not_prove: Renaming is common and often innocent; it does not by itself prove an attempt to hide content.

EXECUTABLE_CONTENT.title: Executable content under another name
EXECUTABLE_CONTENT.shows: The content is a %{detected} program although the name ends in .%{extension}.
EXECUTABLE_CONTENT.does_not_prove: It does not show that the program is malicious; analyse it in an isolated environment.

DUPLICATE.title: Duplicate content
DUPLICATE.does_not_prove: Identical hashes show identical content, not who copied the file or when.

UNREADABLE.title: File could not be read
UNREADABLE.does_not_prove: It does not show that the file is damaged; permissions or locks can cause this.

EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH_WITH_CASE.title: Differs from the evidence registered in the case
EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH_WITH_CASE.shows: The %{algorithm} of this file is %{actual}, but evidence %{evidence_id} was registered at intake with %{expected}: the file examined is not bit-identical to the registered item.
EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH_WITH_CASE.does_not_prove: Who changed the file, when, or whether the change was deliberate; the analysis still ran so the examiner can decide.

EVIDENCE_NOT_IN_CASE_REGISTRY.title: Not registered in the case
EVIDENCE_NOT_IN_CASE_REGISTRY.shows: No item of case %{case_id} was registered with this path or this content, so its continuity from intake cannot be shown.
EVIDENCE_NOT_IN_CASE_REGISTRY.does_not_prove: That the file is altered or irrelevant; it may simply not have gone through intake.

REGISTRY_PATH_CONTENT_CHANGED.title: Registered path now holds different content
REGISTRY_PATH_CONTENT_CHANGED.shows: This path was registered earlier as %{previous_id} with other content; the current content gets a new evidence ID.
REGISTRY_PATH_CONTENT_CHANGED.does_not_prove: Which version is the original or why the content changed.

DKIM_BODY_HASH_MISMATCH.title: DKIM body hash does not match
DKIM_BODY_HASH_MISMATCH.shows: The DKIM signature of %{d} (selector %{s}) records a hash of the message body that differs from the hash of the body as it is now: the body is not the one that was signed.
DKIM_BODY_HASH_MISMATCH.does_not_prove: It does not show who changed the body, when, or why: forwarding systems, mailing lists, antivirus footers and re-encoding by a mail client also change bodies after signing.

DKIM_SIGNATURE_INVALID.title: DKIM signature does not verify
DKIM_SIGNATURE_INVALID.shows: The body still matches the DKIM signature of %{d} (selector %{s}), but the signature over the signed header fields does not verify with the supplied public key (key source: %{key_source}; verifier: %{reason}). Either signed header fields changed after signing, or the supplied key is not the one that signed (for example a rotated key).
DKIM_SIGNATURE_INVALID.does_not_prove: It does not tell which of the two happened, nor who changed a header or why; with a rotated or wrong key a genuine message gives the same result.

DKIM_KEY_FROM_CURRENT_DNS.title: DKIM key taken from today's DNS
DKIM_KEY_FROM_CURRENT_DNS.shows: The key for %{d} (selector %{s}) was not in the examiner's key file and was fetched from the DNS at the time of the analysis (online mode).
DKIM_KEY_FROM_CURRENT_DNS.does_not_prove: A key published today may not be the key that signed the message; a pass or a failure with it says nothing certain about the key valid at sending time.

DKIM_DOMAIN_NOT_ALIGNED.title: Valid DKIM signature from another domain
DKIM_DOMAIN_NOT_ALIGNED.shows: The message carries a valid DKIM signature only for %{d}, which does not share its organisational domain with the From domain %{from_domain}.
DKIM_DOMAIN_NOT_ALIGNED.does_not_prove: Sending services, mailing lists and outsourced mail commonly sign with their own domain; it does not show that the From address was spoofed.

ARC_CHAIN_INVALID.title: ARC chain does not validate
ARC_CHAIN_INVALID.shows: The message has %{instances} ARC set(s) and the chain does not validate (%{reason}).
ARC_CHAIN_INVALID.does_not_prove: An intermediary may have broken the chain, or the keys of the sealers may not have been supplied; it does not show that the message was tampered with.

RECEIVED_TIME_NOT_MONOTONIC.title: Received times go backwards
RECEIVED_TIME_NOT_MONOTONIC.shows: Hop %{hop} was stamped %{hop_date}, %{earlier_by_s} s before the previous hop %{previous_hop} (%{previous_date}), beyond the tolerated clock difference (%{count} such step(s)).
RECEIVED_TIME_NOT_MONOTONIC.does_not_prove: Server clocks are sometimes wrong and some servers add Received headers out of order; it does not show that a header was inserted or edited.

DATE_AFTER_FIRST_HOP.title: Date header later than the first server
DATE_AFTER_FIRST_HOP.shows: The Date header (%{date}) is %{later_by_s} s later than the time the first server received the message (%{first_hop_date}).
DATE_AFTER_FIRST_HOP.does_not_prove: The sender's clock may be wrong; it does not show that the date was changed after sending.

MSG_TRANSPORT_HEADERS_MISSING.title: Outlook message without transport headers
MSG_TRANSPORT_HEADERS_MISSING.shows: The .msg file has no PR_TRANSPORT_MESSAGE_HEADERS property: the original header section (Received hops, DKIM signatures, Authentication-Results) is not available, so DKIM was not attempted.
MSG_TRANSPORT_HEADERS_MISSING.does_not_prove: Drafts, sent items and messages saved by some tools never had these headers; it does not show that they were removed.

ATTACHMENT_DATE_AFTER_SENT.title: Attachment dated after the message
ATTACHMENT_DATE_AFTER_SENT.shows: The %{field} date of attachment %{attachment} (%{attachment_date}) is later than the message Date (%{date}).
ATTACHMENT_DATE_AFTER_SENT.does_not_prove: These dates are written by the sending client and are easy to get wrong or to set freely; it does not show that the attachment was swapped.

LOOKALIKE_DOMAIN.title: Domain resembles an own domain
LOOKALIKE_DOMAIN.shows: The %{header} domain %{domain} (%{domain_unicode}) resembles the own domain %{own_domain} (method: %{method}).
LOOKALIKE_DOMAIN.does_not_prove: Similar names also belong to legitimate, unrelated organisations; it does not show an intent to deceive.

REPLY_TO_DIFFERS.title: Replies go to another organisation
REPLY_TO_DIFFERS.shows: The %{header} address %{address} does not share its organisational domain with the From domain %{from_domain}.
REPLY_TO_DIFFERS.does_not_prove: Help desks, mailing lists, bulk senders and bounce handling legitimately use other addresses; it does not show that replies are being diverted.

DISPLAY_NAME_SPOOF.title: Display name suggests another sender
DISPLAY_NAME_SPOOF.shows: The display name "%{display_name}" of %{address} contains another address or an own-organisation name while the address is external (%{reason}).
DISPLAY_NAME_SPOOF.does_not_prove: People write names freely and partners mention the organisation they work with; it does not show impersonation.

FILE_STRUCTURE_DAMAGED.title: File structure damaged or incomplete
FILE_STRUCTURE_DAMAGED.shows: The %{format} structure is not complete or not well formed (%{problems}); what could be read was analysed.
FILE_STRUCTURE_DAMAGED.does_not_prove: Truncated copies, interrupted exports and non-standard writers cause this too; it does not show deliberate damage.

PARSER_FAILED.title: Message analysis not completed
PARSER_FAILED.shows: The analysis of this message did not complete (reason: %{reason}, exit code %{exit_code}); its email findings are missing.
PARSER_FAILED.does_not_prove: It does not show that the file is malicious or damaged; size limits, time limits and unusual content also stop an analysis.

DKIM_NOT_SIGNED.title: No DKIM signature
DKIM_NOT_SIGNED.shows: The message carries no DKIM-Signature header.
DKIM_NOT_SIGNED.does_not_prove: Many legitimate servers do not sign, and a missing signature is common; it proves nothing about authenticity either way.

DKIM_SIGNATURE_NOT_EVALUATED.title: DKIM signature not evaluated
DKIM_SIGNATURE_NOT_EVALUATED.shows: The DKIM signature of %{d} (selector %{s}) could not be evaluated (%{reason}).
DKIM_SIGNATURE_NOT_EVALUATED.does_not_prove: An expired, unsupported or partial (l=) signature, or a .msg file whose original body is not stored, cannot be checked; it says nothing about the message.

TIMEZONE_INCONSISTENT.title: Time zone inconsistent
TIMEZONE_INCONSISTENT.shows: The Date header uses zone %{date_zone} while the sender organisation's first server used %{hop_zone} (%{reason}).
TIMEZONE_INCONSISTENT.does_not_prove: Clients and servers are often set to different zones, travellers keep their home zone; it does not show that the date was edited.

MESSAGE_ID_DOMAIN_MISMATCH.title: Message-ID from another domain
MESSAGE_ID_DOMAIN_MISMATCH.shows: The Message-ID was generated under %{message_id_domain}, not under the From domain %{from_domain}.
MESSAGE_ID_DOMAIN_MISMATCH.does_not_prove: Mail clients, sending services and webmail hosts generate Message-IDs with their own names; it does not show that the message is forged.

DKIM_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE.title: DKIM key not available
DKIM_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE.shows: No public key for %{name} was supplied, so the signature of %{d} (selector %{s}) could not be checked (offline analysis, no DNS query).
DKIM_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE.does_not_prove: It says nothing about the signature; supply the key that was valid at sending time to check it.

PAYMENT_DETAILS_MENTIONED.title: Payment details mentioned
PAYMENT_DETAILS_MENTIONED.shows: The subject or text mentions payment details: %{terms}.
PAYMENT_DETAILS_MENTIONED.does_not_prove: Invoices and payment notices mention bank details all the time; it is a pointer for review, not a sign of fraud.

DKIM_SIGNATURE_VALID.title: DKIM signature verifies
DKIM_SIGNATURE_VALID.shows: The DKIM signature of %{d} (selector %{s}, %{a}) verifies with the key from %{key_source}: the signed header fields and the body are unchanged since signing.
DKIM_SIGNATURE_VALID.does_not_prove: It shows only that whoever held the private key of %{d} signed this content; it does not show who wrote it, that the From address is truthful, or that unsigned header fields are original.

AUTH_RESULTS_RECORDED.title: Receiving server's checks recorded
AUTH_RESULTS_RECORDED.shows: %{count} Authentication-Results header(s); the top one, written by %{authserv_id}, states: %{results}.
AUTH_RESULTS_RECORDED.does_not_prove: These are claims written into the message by a server; anyone handling the file could have added or edited them, and they were not re-checked.

limitations.SIGNATURE_TABLE_LIMITED: Type detection uses a limited table of common file signatures; unknown types are reported as unknown, not as suspicious.
limitations.TIMESTAMPS_FROM_FILESYSTEM: Modification times come from the file system of the examined copy and may differ from the original source.
limitations.CLEAN_RESULT_IS_NOT_AUTHENTICITY: A result without findings does not prove that a file is authentic or unaltered before acquisition.
limitations.TIMESTAMP_PROVES_EXISTENCE_ONLY: A trusted timestamp proves the audit log existed in this exact form at the stated time; it does not prove that the examined copy matches the original source.
limitations.DKIM_NEEDS_KEY_AT_SENDING_TIME: DKIM results depend on the public keys supplied: a check is only meaningful with the key that was valid when the message was sent. Keys are rotated, so a current key can fail a genuine message and a missing key leaves the signature unchecked.
limitations.MISSING_SIGNATURE_PROVES_NOTHING: A missing DKIM signature is common and proves nothing; a valid signature covers only the signed header fields and the body, not who wrote the message.
limitations.MSG_MAY_LACK_TRANSPORT_HEADERS: Outlook .msg files do not keep the original message: the body is re-encoded (so DKIM cannot be checked) and the original header section is kept only when transport headers were stored.
limitations.BEC_HEURISTICS_FALSE_POSITIVES: Lookalike-domain, Reply-To, display-name and payment-wording checks are heuristics with false positives and false negatives; the organisational domain comes from the bundled Public Suffix List, whose version is recorded in environment.json and may differ from the list in force when the message was sent.
limitations.HEADERS_ARE_CLAIMS: Received, Date and Authentication-Results headers are text that servers and clients wrote; unsigned headers can be added or edited by anyone who handled the file.
limitations.MBOX_ESCAPING_AMBIGUOUS: In an mbox, body lines starting with "From " are escaped with '>'; un-escaping follows the selected variant (mboxrd by default) and cannot always restore the original line, which can affect DKIM body hashes.
